# What to prioritise in the BGL and OpenStack logs

**Scope:** BGL supercomputer logs, 3 June 2005 to 4 January 2006, in Los Angeles time (UTC−7 in summer, UTC−8 in winter). OpenStack cloud logs, 14 to 17 May 2017, in UTC. All components, warnings and worse only.

**Two caveats:**
- **No trend data.** Neither log table has data from before its period, so I can't say whether anything is rising or new. "Change" is "not comparable" for every item [Q60][Q61].
- **Team names are stand-ins.** The owning teams come from a sample ownership table that ships with the tool. They are fictional, not your real org chart [Q30].

**Overall picture:** BGL has 1,012,140 warning-and-worse entries (exact). 626,756 of them are fatal entries from Node OS and 228,536 are fatal entries from HPC Applications [Q62]. OpenStack has only 3,130 such entries, 3,071 of them warnings from Virtualization [Q62]. Almost all the risk is in BGL.

## Top items, most important first

**1. Compute-node kernel crashes reporting an "instruction address" (BGL)**
- **Risk:** compute nodes hit fatal kernel faults across most of the machine and for most of the period.
- **Measured:** ranked 1st of 15. It is fatal, appears on 145 of 213 days with data, and comes from 22,791 distinct hosts, with 47,563 entries (exact) [Q60].
- **Clustering:** the count over all levels is 51,227. About 47,100 of those fall on 13–14 June 2005 and 3,662 on 26 June [Q68], so outside those bursts it's a low, steady background.
- **Component and team:** kernel; Node OS [Q60].
- **Next action:** Node OS to investigate the 13–14 June burst first, then the low daily background, which looks like a separate, ongoing problem.

**2. Fatal kernel entries made of number and hex-code pairs (BGL)**
- **Risk:** a second kind of fatal kernel output that comes back often.
- **Measured:** ranked 2nd of 15. Fatal, on 87 of 213 days, from 2,289 hosts, 16,139 entries (exact) [Q60].
- **Component and team:** kernel; Node OS [Q60].
- **Hypothesis:** these could be the register or diagnostic dumps written alongside the crashes in item 1.
- **Next action:** Node OS to check whether these entries come with item 1's crashes. If they do, handle both as one problem.

**3. The "data TLB error" storm on 11 June 2005 (BGL)**
- **Risk:** the largest single group of fatal entries, but almost all from one day.
- **Measured:** ranked 3rd of 15, with 152,734 entries (exact) on 541 hosts. That is 15.1% of everything ranked in BGL [Q60].
- **Clustering:** 152,182 of them are on 11 June 2005, and no other day has more than 477 [Q68]. These are entries, not separate incidents; this looks like one event.
- **Why it stays 3rd:** its size and spread keep it high, even though it scores 0 on persistence.
- **Next action:** Node OS to look back at what happened on 11 June 2005, and check whether the small repeats in mid-August and late November [Q68] have the same cause.

**4. Jobs failing to start: program image missing, permission denied, login failed, or the connection cut (BGL)**
- **Risk:** user jobs fail at launch.
- **Measured:** five fatal job-launch messages, each on 1,024 hosts [Q60]:

| Message | Entries (exact) | Days present | Rank |
|---|---|---|---|
| Program image missing | 46,416 | 67 | 4th |
| Login failed, no such file | 43,647 | 37 | 5th |
| Program image, permission denied | 43,040 | 27 | 6th |
| Connection to the job "link has been severed" | 26,546 | 35 | 7th |
| Program image, wrong format | 22,032 | 4 | 10th |

- **Component and team:** application layer; HPC Applications [Q60].
- **Hypothesis:** jobs submitted with wrong paths, wrong permissions or wrong binaries, not hardware faults. That would make them cheap to fix.
- **Next action:** HPC Applications to check which jobs and users are behind the "missing" and "permission denied" launches and fix how jobs are submitted.

**5. Control-system assertion failures on a single host (BGL), moved up by me**
- **Risk:** the software that controls the machine hit an internal assertion failure many times.
- **Measured:** 84,250 error entries (exact), but only on 3 of 213 days and from 1 host. Within its team's own ranking it scores 8 of 18 [Q69].
- **Why I moved it up:** it wasn't among the 15 problems the overall ranking considered [Q60]. But it makes up most of Control System's 88,529 error entries [Q62]. The same host also logged 4,276 "packet timeout" errors on 18 days [Q69].
- **Component and team:** control system (MMCS); Control System [Q69].
- **Next action:** Control System to check that one host and the three days of the assertion failures.

**OpenStack, for completeness:** nothing serious. The top item is a warning, "unknown base file" in the image cache: 3,059 entries (exact) in 25 of 30 hours, owned by Virtualization [Q61]. The only critical entries are 2 failures to validate a login token with the identity server, owned by Identity & Access [Q61]. Identity & Access should check them, but they're low priority.

**What the logs don't measure:** customer or user impact, how many jobs were actually lost, downtime, or cost. All counts are log entries, not incidents. The ranking only orders what to look at first; it isn't a measure of risk or impact.

## Evidence

- **[Q30]** Overview of the log tables: time zones, ranges, field roles, and the note that the team names are stand-ins. Both tables, all time, no filters.
  `SELECT … ts_dict_agg("level") … FROM extractor."bgl_search_idx"`

**Scope:** BGL supercomputer logs, 3 June 2005 to 4 January 2006, in Los Angeles time (UTC−7 in summer, UTC−8 in winter). OpenStack cloud logs, 14 to 17 May 2017, in UTC. All components, warnings and worse only.

- **Risk:** compute nodes hit fatal kernel faults across most of the machine and for most of the period.
- **Measured:** ranked 1st of 15. It is fatal, appears on 145 of 213 days with data, and comes from 22,791 distinct hosts, with 47,563 entries (exact) [Q60].
- **Clustering:** the count over all levels is 51,227. About 47,100 of those fall on 13–14 June 2005 and 3,662 on 26 June [Q68], so outside those bursts it's a low, steady background.
- **Component and team:** kernel; Node OS [Q60].

**2. Fatal kernel entries made of number and hex-code pairs (BGL)**
